newsitem.title: USA: Dlr/yen rebounds on Sakakibara, stars at US open.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen rebounds on Sakakibara, stars at US open.

text.p: The dollar opened higher, led by a sharp rebound versus the yen after senior Japanese Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara tried to douse heated concerns about Japan's trade surplus, dealers said.

Traders, expecting further losses in dollar/yen after it touched 110.62 -- a near seven-month low -- Wednesday, were caught short as the dollar jumped after Sakakibara, director general of the Ministry's International Finance Bureau, spoke.
"The world fell apart for all those people who were short dollar/yen. Sakakibara knows how to (move) the market," said David Gilmore, partner at Foreign Exchange Analyics.
The dollar reached a high of 115.70 yen, more than a 4.0 percent gain from its low point Wednesday, before settling to open at 114.03/08 yen, up from 111.27/32 at Wednesday's close.
The dollar opened at 1.7245/55 marks, up from 1.7160/65.
Sakakibara, responding to reporters' questions regarding the market's focus on Japan's trade suplus, said the issue is "being played up excessively."

The influential official also said Japan's trade surplus will not be a major issue at the June 20-22 summit meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations in Denver and reiterated Japan's readiness to combat excessive forex moves.

"A four-yen move overnight certainly gets put in the category of excessive volatility and that's got to be of some concern to the (Japanese) authorities," said Dennis Pettit, foreign exchange manager at Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan.

The dollar sagged a bit after the open on the back of data showing U.S. retail sales declined 0.1 percent in May, in contrast to expectations of a 0.4 percent rise. The Treasury long bond surged a full point after the numbers.
The retail sales drop was the third in a row, coming after revised falls of 0.9 percent in April and 0.3 percent in March.

Analysts said Federal Reserve policy-makers are focusing heavily on consumption and are relatively content that wages are not getting bid up. So the data were helpful for a steady rate outlook after the Fed's July meeting, they said.
Dollar/mark benefitted overnight from mounting hopes that a budget stability pact for European currency union will be signed at the European Union summit next week in Amsterdam.

European Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy helped fan such speculation on Thursday, saying he believed Europe would be able to reach a deal on an accord to limit budget deficits under monetary union.

French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin "was somewhat optimistic as well," said Gilmore. "It seems (European Commission President Jacques) Santer has put together some kind of proposal that will bring all sides together and get the French to endorse the stability pact."
The deal would make more explicit reference to the need to coordinate economic policies across Europe and fight to reduce unemployment, de Silguy said.
The market is now awaiting remarks from U.S. Treasury offcials. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin is scheduled to speak at 1100 EDT/1500 GMT in Washington.
AT 1245 EDT/1645 GMT, Deputy Treasury Secrtary Lawrence Summers is due to speak in Washington.
In other trade, the dollar rose to 1.4440/50 Swiss francs from 1.4385/95 at Wednesday's close. It rose to Canadian $1.3877/82 from C$1.3867/72.
The pound eased to $1.6342/47 from $1.6382/87.
The Australian dollar opened at $0.7504/09.
((-- Alden Bentley, NY Treasury Desk, 212 859 1667))
